questions: What is the 4 in 3 452 worth, and why?
What happens when the ones column collects ten ones?
segments.say: Thousands, hundreds, tens, ones. Name each place in 3 452 as the digits drop into their columns, then watch ten ones regroup into one ten. Keep your student notes open at the place value definition for this scene.

questions: Why do we start adding from the ones, not the hundreds?
Where did the carried hundred in 247 + 385 come from?
segments.say: Addition with regrouping: 247 + 385. Add column by column from the ones and narrate both regroupings as the chips appear. Now try the addition question on the worksheet in pairs.

questions: Why can we not take 7 ones away from 2 ones straight away?
Does borrowing change the value of 632? How do you know?
segments.say: Subtraction with regrouping: 632 − 247. Narrate both borrows slowly - a ten for the ones, then a hundred for the tens. Check the regrouping definition in your student notes.

questions: How many groups are there, and how many dots in each group?
How is 4 x 3 the same as 3 + 3 + 3 + 3?
segments.say: Multiplication is repeated addition. Watch four groups of three dots gather into one array and follow the counting probe. Compare this with the multiplication definition in your student notes.

questions: Why must we do the addition before the subtraction here?
What regrouping happened when 45 and 25 were added?
segments.say: One worked example: 45 + 25 − 30. Work left to right with the class - add 25 to reach 70, then give 30 away to land on 40. Finish the mixed question on the worksheet now.

questions: What does the zero in 5 0 6 7 do?
What goes wrong if we drop the zero?
segments.say: Misconception: the zero in 5 0 6 7 holds its place. Contrast the correct reading five thousand and sixty-seven with the wrong reading 567, then land the place-holding rule. Finish by taking the exit ticket on your own - its first question revisits exactly this trap.
segments.watchFor: Reading 5 0 6 7 as 567, skipping the zero. Listen and look for it in pair talk and on the worksheet: any reading of 5 0 6 7 as 567 shows the trap - send them back to scene s6 and to the correct turn: Zero holds its place: 5 0 6 7 is five thousand and sixty-seven, with the 0 keeping the hundreds empty.
